```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The deciding factor is the 90-day window. B's own best evidence, dashp's founder account, puts the sales cycle at about 5 months of in-person trust-building per closed deal. That alone overruns the target. B's backup channel is a PestWorld booth, and the 2026 booths are already sold out.",
    "A has a sourced, fast, self-serve channel. Meta lead ads in Career & Employment cost about $12.30 per lead (LocalIQ), and Google CPL is falling year over year (WordStream). A solo operator can run these immediately, without months of relationship selling.",
    "A's price points are anchored to live, published tiers: Kickresume at $8–24/mo and WeGoUp at $9.99/mo. An individual can pay by card on the spot with no procurement step, which suits a first-dollar goal.",
    "A's build fits a solo operator with AI agents: a bounded text pipeline with near-zero marginal cost. B's MVP would have to match D2DHQ's attrition, escrow and QuickBooks logic and plug into CRM/payroll systems the owner controls. That is harder and slower to integrate.",
    "B's strongest pro-evidence (dashp at ~$100k ARR) also shows its market is crowded. dashp is itself a direct competitor, and another solo builder is pitching an almost identical tool. B's addressable market is described as only 'hundreds' of companies, so each lost deal matters more."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence does not come from the payer. Both quotes, an anonymous complaint-site post and one litigated $217k commission dispute, show reps being underpaid by employers. Neither shows a pest control owner or sales-ops manager, the stated payer, wanting or paying for tracking software. If anything, the evidence suggests owners may benefit from the opacity the product would remove.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A has real weaknesses: free direct competitors such as GapZero, a one-time need that caps lifetime value, and an unverified free-to-paid conversion rate. Its demand quotes show anxiety, not willingness to pay for gap-framing specifically. A wins mainly because B's sourced sales-cycle evidence conflicts directly with the 90-day goal. B could be the better long-term business if the 5-month cycle turns out to be unrepresentative."
}
```
